WIKI.title: Drill bit sizes (number and letter gauge tables)
WIKI.note: The article says the gauge-to-diameter relation is not defined by a formula and that ASME B94.11M lists number sizes to 97.

STOODY.title: Decimal equivalents: drills, taps, dies (catalogue page 444)
STOODY.note: K printed as .2610 (the same as G; out of sequence between J .2770 and L .2900). O printed as .3150. Metric list read where an inch value was printed on the same line; 9.8 appears twice (against .3504 and .3858), the first is taken as a misprint of 8.9.

LOBBEN.title: Machinists' and Draftsmen's Handbook, p. 148: Table 19 twist drill numbers 1 to 80; Table 20 letter sizes
LOBBEN.note: Public-domain book (Project Runeberg scan). The OCR lost the letter on the row between P (.323) and N (.302); recorded as O by its position.

WIKI_ISO.title: ISO metric screw thread (table of preferred sizes, coarse and fine pitches, from ISO 262)

OPTIMAS_M.title: ISO Metric Thread Dimensions (coarse and fine tables)
OPTIMAS_M.note: Lists ISO 261 sizes including second and third choices; fine list read to M24 x 1.5. Basic dimensions printed: M17x1 d3 printed 15.733 (formula 15.773) and M48 D1 printed 42.857 (formula 42.587) look like transpositions; all other checked values agree with ISO 68-1 formulas to 0.001 mm. Its tap drill column is major minus pitch.

WIKI_UTS.title: Unified Thread Standard (main size table)
WIKI_UTS.note: Number-size formula printed: major diameter = number x 0.013 in + 0.060 in. Names ASME B1.1-2024.

OPTIMAS_UN.title: UNC, UNF and UNEF Thread Table

OPTIMAS_TOL.title: ISO Metric Screw Thread Tolerances (coarse table, external 6g)
OPTIMAS_TOL.note: Header note 'Tolerances 6g (6h)'; M1 to M1.4 are printed with zero allowance (6h). M2.5 pitch max printed 2.118 (Ganter and the formula: 2.188).

GANTER_13.title: Metric ISO threads, tolerance fields 6g / 6H (DIN 13 extract, technical information 2393)
GANTER_13.note: Values with decimal commas. The M2.5 row could not be aligned reliably by the page reader; its external values 2.480/2.380/2.188/2.117 are recorded.

CDE_6H.title: Nuts: internal threads, class 6H, DIN 13; ISO 68 & ISO R 1501 (June 2000)

WIKI_IT.title: IT Grade (article, table of IT values)
WIKI_IT.note: IT01 to IT11 printed in um, IT12 to IT18 in mm (converted to um here, x1000).

GANTER_IT.title: DIN ISO 286 ISO-Grundtoleranzen, Auszug Teil 1 Zahlenwerte (technical appendix p. 2150)
GANTER_IT.note: Printed in um with decimal commas. IT18 over 315 to 400 printed as 2200, out of sequence with its neighbours (8100, 9700); recorded as printed.

GOST_25346.title: GOST 25346-89 Unified system of tolerances and fits, Tables 2 and 3 (national adoption of ISO 286-1:1988)
GOST_25346.note: Table 2 (shafts) and Table 3 (holes, page 65935_3/_4, including the delta values). Merged cells cover the main size step; recorded on the main step. f over 30 to 40 printed '25' without its sign in the transcription (column is negative); recorded as -25.

ROYMECH.title: ISO shaft fundamental deviations 0 to 500 mm
ROYMECH.note: The site does not permit substantial reproduction, so its table is not republished here. It was compared value by value with the GOST 25346 transcription for letters a to zc (except j, js, k): all 517 printed values are equal. Only its k column is recorded.

SIMPLYB.title: FAQ / ISO 286 Limits and Fits reference (shaft and hole limit deviations, ISO 286-2)
SIMPLYB.note: Prints limit deviations of tolerance classes for 3 to 400 mm. The fundamental deviation is read as the limit nearest zero of the class named in 'from'. f6 over 120 to 180 printed -43/-48 (lower limit inconsistent with f5/f7; the upper, fundamental, value -43 is unaffected).

OSG_JIS.title: Deviation of shafts to be used in commonly used fits (JIS B 0401 extract)
OSG_JIS.note: JIS B 0401 is the Japanese adoption of ISO 286. Prints limit deviations up to 250 mm; fundamental deviation read as the limit nearest zero.
